reasoning: I found no check anywhere between the vendor's JSON and Int(). (1) Source: AnthropicWireTypes.swift:71 decodes `utilization` through flexibleDoubleIfPresent (AppConfig.swift:199-203). That helper is a plain Double decode with no range or isFinite check, so a finite value like 1e300 is accepted. toSnapshot (AnthropicWireTypes.swift:140-147) passes the value into UsageWindow as is, and UsageWindow.init (UsageWindow.swift:15-20) stores it unchanged. (2) Persistence: VendorViewModel.swift:235 calls recordHistory(snapshot.maxUtilization), which reaches UsageHistoryStore.append (UsageHistoryStore.swift:56-58). append encodes the raw Double. JSONEncoder only rejects non-finite values, and 1e300 is finite, so it is written to disk. load (UsageHistoryStore.swift:92-125) decodes it back and only filters by timestamp. (3) Aggregation: computePeakDay (AnalyticsAggregator.swift:29-47) takes the per-day max() with no clamp and returns it as utilizationPercent. AnalyticsAggregator.swift:121 and :157 put that result into summary.peakDay. (4) Sink: VendorAnalyticsCardView.swift:143-145 renders AnalyticsFormatters.peakDayText. At AnalyticsFormatters.swift:46 and :48 it calls Int(record.utilizationPercent), and Int() of a Double at or above about 9.22e18 traps at runtime. The only isFinite check in the model layer (UsageSnapshot.swift:325) is on a different path, notifications above 90%, and there is no clamp in Providers, History or the aggregator. I found no framework, type-system or middleware protection. Whether a malicious vendor or TLS MITM is a realistic attacker is a question for the REACHABILITY lens. It does not change that nothing on this path would stop the crash.
